subject: Noon surge exception and prorata settlement
messages:
From: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@orbishealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orbishealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Urgent: noon surge — short-window quota increase request

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from our platform team: we have a marketing push that will spike generation traffic between 12:30–14:30 ET tomorrow (expected ~3x current peak for ~90 minutes). We need a short-window increase to avoid throttles — ideally a 2x quota lift for that window.

Two asks:
- Can you enable a provisional quota increase for that 2-hour window with immediate effect?
- How will billing work for the excess tokens/throughput — we need clear language for our procurement team (PO + invoice). Is a prorated true-up possible and can Redwood provide any goodwill credit given this is an unplanned launch?

We can share an immediate PO if that speeds things up. Please loop in whoever owns billing.

Thanks,
Alicia Chen
Head of Platform, OrbisHealth
Alicia.Chen@orbishealth.com

---
Attachment: launch-plan.pdf (summary, 220KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 16:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Urgent: noon surge — short-window quota increase request

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up.

We can definitely enable a short-window uplift. Proposed approach:
- Immediate provisional uplift activated for 2026-06-22 12:30–14:30 ET (2 hours).
- Capacity: temporary throughput/headroom to cover ~3x current peak (we'll set a safety buffer; I'll confirm the exact token/sec ceiling).
- Billing: we'll prorate based on the hourly uplift rate and include any overage as a one-line true-up on your next invoice.

On credits: we can offer a one-time 20% credit on the billed overage for this incident conditional on a signed short amendment (covers this event only). Ben and Monica are cc'd to detail the billing mechanics and get procurement-friendly language.

If you can send an immediate PO number I can kick off the uplift and route the amendment for signature (DocuSign).

Karthik
Head of Sales (Developer Platforms)
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@orbishealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Urgent: noon surge — short-window quota increase request

Alicia — looping in the billing specifics. Per the plan above, here are the pricing mechanics we will apply for this type of one-off uplift:

1) Uplift billing model
- Hourly prorated uplift fee = (monthly committed token rate unit price) * uplift factor prorated to hours used.
- Any usage above your committed capacity during the uplift window is billed as overage at the agreed overrun rate (we'll provide a line-item).

2) Goodwill/credit
- For this incident we will apply a one-time 20% credit to overage charges if the signed amendment is returned within 72 hours.

3) Documentation & invoice flow
- We will attach a short amendment (1 page) that describes the uplift window, the uplift cap, and the credit terms. Once signed, the uplift is considered authorized and will appear as an invoice line item "June 22 emergency uplift" on your next invoice dated Jul 1.

Attached: provisional_uplift_pricing.xlsx (hourly estimates and sample invoice rows) and a small usage export template we can fill after the event (usage-report-jun21.csv).

Next steps I propose:
- Alicia: send PO# now (even a short email PO) to speed activation.
- Karthik: I'll prepare the amendment and DocuSign link; Monica will confirm GL code and invoice recipient.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
